A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

shade-tolerant and shade-intolerant conifers have similar growth responses to light, but shade-tolerant species are less sensitive to light and may grow rapidly under a wider range of light environments than are shade-intolerant species.
the response of conifer saplings to light is complex and contingent upon age, size and species.
the most shade-tolerant species are most likely to grow in the understory and least likely to respond to thinning, whereas the most shade-intolerant species may respond most dramatically to thinning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
growth of shade-intolerant conifers is resource-limited and depends on light and other resources, but the specific relationships are species- and size-specific.
the response of conifer saplings to light varies among species, and the response is often dependent on age or size of the sapling.
